clue.text: Brew crewmen hot tea on Loire

blocks.note: ABs are able seamen, members of a ship's crew
hot, as in fashionable, is 'in'
thé is French for tea, as drunk on the Loire

explanation.surface: Sailors are making a cup of tea while on the river Loire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Loire is a French river, so it signals a French word: THE without its accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong aniseed-flavoured spirit, and brew is a loose word for any prepared drink.

clue.text: Loaded issue covers flap

blocks.note: to issue forth, as water from the ground, is to well
a flap or fuss is a to-do

explanation.surface: A magazine issue has a cover story about some flap.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the first piece sits on top of, and so covers, the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for rich, which is what well-to-do means.

clue.text: The thing: can it do very well?

definitions.text: The thing: can it do very well?

blocks.clueFragment: The thing: can it do very well?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone sizing up a gadget and wondering whether it will perform
setter's reading: a body that can perform very well physically is fit, in good condition

explanation.surface: Someone doubtfully examines an object, asking whether it will be any good.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as about a gadget's quality; it is really about physical fitness, the state of being able to do very well at exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in good physical condition, fit enough to perform well, is the two-word phrase in the grid.

clue.text: Guys supporting regularly patch up cute property

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the following words is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words
guys are men

explanation.surface: Men are helping to mend something cute, perhaps a pretty cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece supporting another sits below it. Cute here means shrewd, not sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its older sense means shrewd, and acumen is shrewdness, the quality a cute person has.

clue.text: Hang insurgent, large stake?

indicators.note: an insurgent is rising up, and in a down answer rising up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: large means big
a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: A rebel is to be hanged, with a big wager on the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Insurgent looks like a noun for a rebel but works as an instruction to turn the first piece upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows, and as a verb to gibbet someone is to hang them.

clue.text: Activity of those coaching masseuse and showing passion

blocks.note: a masseuse rubs, so is a rubber
necking is kissing passionately

explanation.surface: A sports coach is training a masseuse while getting emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaching is not training but riding on a coach tour, whose passengers crane their necks to gawp at sights.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbernecking is gawping at sights, as coach-trip tourists do, twisting their necks to look around.

clue.text: Film tank tracks

blocks.note: a reservoir is a tank for storing water
to dog someone is to track them

explanation.surface: A film about a tank, or the tracks a tank runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 crime movie, his debut feature.

clue.text: Bolt inspires European, super muscular athlete once

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the first word takes the next inside it

blocks.note: to bolt food is to gorge
E is the abbreviation for European
a super, or superintendent, is a foreman

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, the sprinter, inspires a muscular European athlete of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt reads as the Jamaican sprinter but is the verb for wolfing food.
explanation.definitionFit: George Foreman was a heavyweight boxing champion of the 1970s and 1990s, a powerfully built sportsman now retired.

clue.text: A West Country lass hasn't started describing Eddy

indicators.note: not having started means the word is missing its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the West Country is in the South West of England
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl from Somerset or Devon is giving a description of someone called Eddy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddy has a capital to look like a name; it is a swirl of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswirl means swirling round, the motion that describes an eddy in water or air.

clue.text: Maybe singer clutches this particular chap, youngster from up north reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are judged by how they are pronounced

blocks.note: him points at one particular man
a buck is a young man, and in a northern English accent the word sounds like book

explanation.surface: A singer is clinging to a particular man, a young lad from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern English accents give buck the vowel of book. A hymnbook is something a churchgoing singer might hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer in church typically holds a hymnbook, the volume of hymns, so it is an example of what one clutches.

clue.text: Parents periodically recalled meal

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept
recalled means called back, so the kept letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad now and then remember a meal they once had.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or early evening meal in Britain, often the main evening meal in the north.

clue.text: Good bouncer catches empty threat: Cave!

indicators.note: empty means the inside has gone, leaving only the outside letters
to catch something is to hold it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a kangaroo, or roo, bounces
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer hears an idle threat and cries 'Cave!', the old schoolboy warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave! is Latin for 'beware' in British school slang, but here it is simply a hollow in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Different IDs used to obtain ordinary English wine

blocks.note: a PIN, a personal identification number, is one kind of ID
O is the abbreviation for ordinary
a name tag is a different kind of ID
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone used fake identity cards to buy a bottle of plain English wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Different IDs asks for two kinds of identification, one placed each side of the ordinary letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinotage is a red grape variety from South Africa and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Quartet missing first of Telegraph setters?

indicators.note: missing its first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a quartet is four

explanation.surface: A group of four Telegraph crossword compilers lacks its leading member.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the setters' own voice: what belongs to the Telegraph setters is, to them, ours.
explanation.definitionFit: A Telegraph setter speaking of the setters' own things would use the possessive 'our', meaning belonging to us.

clue.text: Jose cycling stops big noise, adjusting hooter

indicators.note: cycling means the letters go round, the first moving to the end
to stop a hole is to plug it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a nob is an important person, a big noise
the J moves from front to back

explanation.surface: Jose rides his bike to stop a loud noise while fixing a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is British slang for the nose as well as a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose job is cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, so it adjusts one's hooter.

clue.text: Black fly

blocks.note: first meaning: deep glossy black
second meaning: to travel by ... aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a dark insect; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is both an intensely black colour, named after the black stone, and a verb meaning to travel by jet plane.

clue.text: Following struggle, remove block

blocks.note: a war is a struggle
to doff a hat is to remove it

explanation.surface: After a fight, someone takes away an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: Following says the second piece comes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off an attack or blow is to fend it off, to block it.

clue.text: Going north, some mayonnaise travels well

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing a kind of well

indicators.note: going north in a down answer means reading upwards
some means part of the following words, so the letters are inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Mayonnaise is being taken north and survives the journey well.
explanation.walkthrough: Travels well is a stock phrase about food surviving a journey; well is the noun for a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well is one where pressure pushes the water up without pumping, so artesian names a type of well.

clue.text: Catch and swill small fish

blocks.note: to swill a drink is to down it
S is the abbreviation for small
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler catches some little fish and washes them down.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch looks like a verb for angling but is the noun for a hidden snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden drawback, which is what a downside is.

clue.text: An ordained minister visiting tipped eatery

indicators.note: tipped over in a down answer means turned upside down, so read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
Rev, for Reverend, is the title of an ordained minister
visiting someone is being at their place

explanation.surface: A clergyman pays a visit to a restaurant, leaving a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipped looks like leaving a gratuity in an eatery; it means tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or tavern, so an eatery.

clue.text: French relations see you serving in trattoria?

blocks.note: FR is the abbreviation for French
relations as in sexual relations, which is IT
ta-ta is a casual goodbye, like see you

explanation.surface: French relatives say goodbye while working as waiters in an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Serving is a noun, a portion of food, not working as a waiter; the question mark flags that a frittata is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A frittata is an Italian open omelette, a dish one might be served in an Italian trattoria.

clue.text: Rates reserve musician's repeated melody

definitions.note: plural noun; a tariff is a list of rates

blocks.note: the TA, or Territorial Army, is the British Army reserve
a riff is a short repeated phrase in music

explanation.surface: Someone judges whether a musician's repetitive tune is worth holding back.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates looks like a verb for judging; it is the plural noun for charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of charges, so it sets out rates for goods or services.

clue.text: A garden sculpture shifting to where workers gather

indicators.note: shifting means moving away, so those two letters are taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
topiary is hedge clipped into ornamental shapes

explanation.surface: A statue in a garden is being moved to where staff meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Workers are worker bees, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are kept, so worker bees gather there.

clue.text: Retired wife at TT dressed OTT

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, describing showy dress

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol: dry

explanation.surface: A wife who has left work turns up at the TT motorbike races in flashy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: TT reads as the Isle of Man motorbike race but stands for teetotal. OTT is 'over the top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means showy but cheap and in poor taste, as clothes worn over the top would be.

clue.text: Jockey, the sixth finisher in race

indicators.note: the finisher of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
the finisher, or final letter

explanation.surface: A jockey came home sixth in a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: Jockey reads as a rider; as a verb it means to compete for position.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey for position is to compete for it, which is to vie.

clue.text: Forceful ex-Olympian runs with audible strain

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the word is judged by its pronunciation

blocks.note: Sebastian Coe, the British middle-distance runner who won Olympic golds
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to strain liquid is to sieve it

explanation.surface: A former Olympic runner competes while visibly and noisily struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Strain reads as an athlete's effort but means filtering with a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercive means using force or threats to make someone act, so it is forceful.

clue.text: When Mum's back inside, view Street on TV

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backwards direction
inside means one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: to view is to see
Ma's, Mum's possessive

explanation.surface: When Mum returns home, she watches Coronation Street on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the word that comes before Street in the TV title, the children's show Sesame Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame Street is the long-running American children's programme, so sesame is the word paired with Street on television.

clue.text: Yellowish sickly sandwiches left outside in dire town

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letter, the ones kept
a sandwich has filling between its slices, so one word holds the next

blocks.note: saffron is an orange-yellow colour
wan means pale and sickly
L is the abbreviation for left
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A jaundiced-looking person eating sandwiches is stranded in a grim town.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwiches looks like food but signals one piece going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron Walden is a market town in north-west Essex, England, named for its historic saffron crop.
